content.value_statement: Client-side vulnerabilities can expose users through unsafe rendering, navigation, and browser integrations. This skill provides practical guidance for secure frontend implementation and verification.
actual_capabilities: Identifies safer DOM APIs for rendering dynamic text and untrusted content.
Recommends established sanitization libraries for permitted HTML content.
Guides Content Security Policy design, staged deployment, and violation reporting.
Reviews URL handling, redirects, external links, and iframe integrations.
Covers browser controls including Trusted Types, SRI, CORP, and COEP.
Suggests secure frontend patterns for authentication, service workers, and third-party widgets.
limitations: Provides guidance only and does not execute scanners or test a running application.
Requires project context to produce framework-specific and deployment-ready recommendations.
Client-side controls cannot replace server-side validation, authorization, or output encoding.
The referenced implementation playbook is not included in the scanned package.

use_cases.title: Secure a rendering feature
use_cases.description: Choose safe DOM APIs and sanitization boundaries for user-controlled text or permitted HTML.

use_cases.title: Plan browser defenses
use_cases.description: Define CSP, Trusted Types, SRI, framing, and cross-origin controls for an application.

use_cases.title: Review an integration
use_cases.description: Evaluate redirects, authentication flows, widgets, payment forms, or service workers before release.

prompt_templates.title: Secure dynamic text rendering
prompt_templates.prompt: Review how [untrusted content] is rendered in [framework]. Explain the XSS risk and recommend safe DOM APIs.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs guidance for displaying user-controlled text.

prompt_templates.title: Design safe rich-text handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe rich-text rendering flow for [application]. Include sanitization boundaries, allowed content, URL validation, and test cases.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer must support limited user-authored HTML.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a staged CSP rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged Content Security Policy for [application architecture]. Cover report-only deployment, nonces or hashes, third-party sources, reporting, and compatibility testing.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs browser protections without disrupting production.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a complete frontend feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [frontend feature] for XSS, open redirects, clickjacking, token exposure, and third-party risks. Propose prioritized fixes and verification steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced reviewer needs a focused implementation assessment.

output_examples.input: We display customer names with innerHTML. What should change?
output_examples.output: Use a text-only DOM API for names, remove HTML interpretation, and add tests with markup-like input to confirm safe rendering.

output_examples.input: Our site needs a CSP without breaking third-party payments.
output_examples.output: Start in report-only mode, inventory required origins, prefer nonces or hashes, validate the payment integration, then enforce the tested policy.

output_examples.input: Users can submit formatted biographies with links.
output_examples.output: Sanitize permitted HTML with an established library, restrict URLs and attributes, keep sanitization near the rendering boundary, and test bypass payloads.

best_practices: Provide the framework, data source, trust boundary, and browser requirements with each request.
Treat server validation, authorization, and secure headers as required companions to frontend controls.
Deploy policies gradually, collect violations, and verify expected workflows before enforcement.
anti_patterns: Do not insert untrusted values through HTML-parsing DOM APIs without established sanitization.
Do not build custom sanitizers when a maintained, well-tested library meets the requirement.
Do not store sensitive session tokens in browser storage without evaluating exposure and application architecture.

faq.question: Does this skill execute security tools?
faq.answer: No. It contains guidance for analysis, implementation, and verification, but no executable scanner or automation.

faq.question: Can it replace a penetration test?
faq.answer: No. Use dedicated testing and expert review for environment-specific assurance.

faq.question: Which frontend frameworks does it support?
faq.answer: Its browser security principles are framework-neutral. Provide framework details for more specific recommendations.

faq.question: Can it secure server-side behavior?
faq.answer: It can identify related requirements, but backend validation, authorization, headers, and session controls need separate implementation.

faq.question: How does it handle permitted HTML?
faq.answer: It recommends established sanitization libraries, explicit content rules, safe URL handling, and tests for bypass attempts.

faq.question: Is the referenced implementation playbook included?
faq.answer: No. The scanned package contains only SKILL.md, so detailed guidance must come from the main skill content.
